Welcome to Warhamer 40k, or as we'll call it w40k, it has six races, each with their own name classes, units, and heroes.  And then we have the.... <pause and slide that to the side.>

This is Warhammer 40k, but it's not.  Instead this is a third person hack and slash, with ranged weapons where you play a Space Marine (or an Ultramarine) and fight through 18 stages.  It is in the 40k universe, but it doesn't require the massive wealth of knowledge or fandom most of these games seem to expect. 

And you know what?  It's the first Warhammer 40k game I really really enjoyed.   Dawn of War is a fine RTS if you really want to play an RTS, or really want to deal with that complexity, however Space Marine brings the user into the universe and creates a reasonable scope of the world for them to enjoy. 

It avoid overly repetitive gameplay, it avoids the massively complex world of 40k which will overwhelm all but the few fans of sci fi with the ability to comprehend it all from a game, and focuses on just a single adventure in that universe. 

And it works!   The gameplay is fantastic, where the main character has a decent amount of options.  You can choose from three weapons, and a number of ranged weapons (carrying up to 4 at a time, with I believe at least 7 different weapons, not counting full upgrades).   The enemies is a little similar, for a majority of the game you will fight the orks (one of the six races)  but there's enough variety in location, ability and configurations that it rarely feels like a slog, surprisingly so. 

Even the graphics hold up well for a 6 year old (last gen) game.   The story is solid.  It's not going to win awards, but it at least has a driving force and while it does dig a bit into the lore (at least i think it does) isn't a distracting trip.  If you like the lore, I'm sure you'll get a lot out of it, but if you don't know the lore at a deep level (like me) you'll really enjoy the story. 

Overall I like the game, I like the game a lot more than quite a few game.  It's definitely trying to be a bit like that "god of war" style that everyone was playing at the time, quite a bit of hack and slash is required, though this game finds a solid balance between third person shooting and melee fighting and it's pretty glorious when you have it right.    I recommend it, and considering it's often on sales, it's a great time to pick this up.

I rather enjoyed this and I must admit, having played a number of Warhammer 40k games throughout the years this is the only one I've gone through that captured a fraction of the atmosphere and "flavour" of the 40k universe. It's not something I can easily describe, but clearly the developers Relic have an understanding of the universe and the factions within. For the most part the characters, the way they are written and the way they reacted to the games plot and situations was very .. "warhmmer"  and it was stronger for that in my mind.

One thing this game absolutely nailed was the scale. The size of the Space Marines versus normal humans, the power armour was correctly proportioned and detailed in all the rght ways, the weapons are the correct sizes, the vehicles, buildings, aliens... everything was bang on as far as I am concerned when it came to scale.

In truth I can't really fault the game too much. It had to step away from the lore a bit to fit in game mechanics, for example a Space Marine Captain (leader of a 100 strong Space Marine Company, veteran of centuries of warfare) wouldn't turn up to battle with just 2 fellow Space Marines in tow..  armed with a standard Bolter and Combat knife, but that had to be done for progression of course... by the end of the game I had a personal force field (Iron halo), a selection of around 7 different firearms, and a choice between a chain sword, power axe and a blummin' two handed thunder hammer. Not really correct in the world...  but makes sense in a game.

The game itself was good fun, melee combat was well done, although an ability to parry would have been nice, and the gun play felt very heavy and dangerous. They got the feel and sound of a Bolter just as I imagine it, bang on the money, and at times I really felt like I was playing a real Space Marine from the stories and board games.

The main critism has to be the checkpoint system. Some poorly placed checkpoints sapped a little joy from the experience, mainly the one's that were frequently placed before an unskippable in engine cutscene... which generally pre-empted a major engagement  you could easily lose.... only to then repeat the whole scene again when the you're plonked back at the checkpoint. That wasn't good.

However that last point aside, an enjoyable game and glad I finally played it!

[h1]They are my bulwark against the Terror. They are the Defenders of Humanity. They are my Space Marines, and they shall know no fear.[/h1]

[h1]Introduction[/h1]
To my sincerest detriment, I don’t know that much about the Warhammer universe. Space Marine was my first excursion into the world, and I wasn’t sure what to expect. I know the lore can be dense and somewhat overwhelming, so I stepped into it cautiously and found myself entirely encapsulated by the characters, story and world that was building around me.

[table]
[tr]
 [th][b]🟩 Positives[/b][/th]
 [th][b]🟥 Negatives[/b][/th]
[/tr]
[tr]
 [td]🟩 A well-written and detailed story experience that allows you to dip your toes into the universe without feeling overwhelmed.

🟩 Fun, fast-paced combat sequences that enable easy combinations of melee and ranged attacks.

🟩 Despite its age, the graphics and audio quality are substantially good, with only minor issues marring the experience. [/td]
 [td]🟥 The boss encounters are not challenging and do not differentiate from normal combat in any way. [/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

[h1]Story[/h1]
A million-strong Ork invasion of Forge World Graia forces Imperial Commanders to deploy a group of Space Marines to the planet's surface to reinforce the local military and reclaim the critically important manufacturing facilities and what they house before the Ork war machine can consume it.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3326868445

You are Captain Titus, the head of the Space Marine group, and it is your responsibility to assist the ground forces where possible and push back the Ork army at any cost.

But what cost will be too high to pay? What will the Orks take from you in their conquest? And what other forces are at play on the surface of this world?

[h1]Gameplay Analysis[/h1]
[h3]"It is better to die for the Emperor, than to live for yourself"[/h3]
Maneuverability and combat are the main staples of your experience in Space Marine. You will spend most of your time navigating the battlefield, positioning yourself in and out of enemy fire, and combating the enemy forces with a whole arsenal of weaponry.

The game has smooth and seamless movement mechanics that allow you to swiftly move between covers and get the advantage over the enemy forces.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3326868625

On top of the clean movement, the combat has also been streamlined in both aspects of its performance. Ranged combat which consists of firing guns of all types into enemy faces that effectively turns them into red mist, is extremely satisfying and feels impactful with every round you let loose. Melee combat is also rewarding, but at the cost of higher damage you are putting yourself under fire, and that doesn't often lead to the desired outcome, especially on higher difficulties.

Thankfully, as a Space Marine, you have quite a large threshold for damage absorption and it will take quite a lot to bring you down. A decent pool of health and an ever-replenishing shield makes it exceptionally easy to stay alive assuming that is your goal.

[h3]"Serve the Emperor today, tomorrow you may be dead."[/h3]
Multiplayer is the only other large concept in Space Marine, and to be honest it's largely dead. I was able to find a few games and it consisted of 90% level-capped players dominating the field and the occasional victory based on events outside of my control. Most of the achievements can be attained through private matches though and if you have someone willing to help, it can be done quite easily and quickly.

On top of the lack of players, the multiplayer servers are still extremely buggy, and the lag is awful to endure for long periods.

[h1]Audio and Visual[/h1]
For a game released in 2011, Space Marine still holds up to this day. The graphics are far from cutting-edge and it would be a true crime to say they are beautiful, but I'm genuinely surprised by how good this game still looks despite its age.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3326868960

The audio is another large-scale surprise for me. It's far from perfect and still has been marred by its age, but it's still generally well-done from the heavy footfalls of your character to the visceral grinding of your chainsword saying hello to the squishy Orks.

[h1]Performance and Specifications[/h1]
You won't have much issue running this game, the minimum requirements are fairly low and don't seem to have ever been a very resource-hungry experience.
RAM: 32GB 3200GHz G-Skill (DDR4)
CPU: i9 10900KA 3.70GHz
GPU: MSI Ventus RTX 3080

[h1]Final Thoughts - Very Good[/h1]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2529084785]Review chart here.[/url]
Despite my reservations and cautious attempt of stepping into Space Marine, I had a lot of fun playing this game and I feel like it was the perfect catalyst for getting into the universe of 40K. It's far from a flawless game, as it has definitely felt the impacts of its age from a gameplay and aesthetic standpoint and isn't a particularly long title for what can still be a $75 game at full price, but if you can get it cheap, I would highly recommend playing this title.

[h1]TL;DR? See Conclusion[/h1]

[h1]INTRODUCTION:[/h1]
We have all seen big men, wearing big armor, wielding big guns and doing manly stuff from previous games (like Gears of War or Star Craft), but have you ever wondered who started it all?

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is a Third Person Hack, Slash and Shooter game developed by Relic Entertainment who has constantly delivered quality work when dealing with the Warhammer 40k universe.

[h1]STORY (No Spoilers):[/h1]
You play as Captain Titus of the Ultramarines, along side his friend Sidonus and the newly initiated Leandros, all of whom are sent to the forge world of Gaira with the objective of protecting a Warlord Class Titan from being looted by a full Ork Invasion. Unknown to Captain Titus, however...other forces are at work there.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
+ [b]Visuals (as a whole):[/b] -This game boast beautiful cut scenes, epic scenery, massive buildings and intense combat. Model and Animation quality are very well made which is complemented by its superior sound quality. The violence in this game is extreme and oddly very satisfying.

+ [b]Audio:[/b] -From the soundtrack to the footsteps and  bolter or lasgun fire, Relic has performed admirably on the sound assets which greatly improves the immersion experience. The voice acting delivered by Mark Strong as Captain Titus is great and complemented by the performance of the supporting cast.

+ [b]Story:[/b] -The game offers a linear story progression which contains enough lore to satisfy the old school and long time fans of the Warhammer 40k Universe, but at the same time, is easy enough to comprehend and understand for the new comers. Story is around 8 to 9 hours long, and 6-7 if you have already played it once. The difficulty level of the game does merit a replay.

+ [b]Multiplayer:[/b] -I normally don't consider multiplayer because I'm a singleplayer oriented gamer but I was able to substantially play the multiplayer mode of Space Marine and was impressed. Multiple game modes and heavy customization really is a big bonus here.

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
- [b]Texture Quality:[/b] -Although I said that visuals AS A WHOLE is good, the texture quality of this game is quite inferior. It may have looked good on the console versions but on the PC on 1080p, one can see that the textures used was only low res. The poor lip syncing was also a minor annoyance for me. The Artstyle is great but it does not excuse low resolution textures specially on the PC.

- [b]Terrible PC Settings:[/b] -This game should have had a more extensive PC settings instead of the generic preset of “low-medium-high”. I feel that devs who does not put effort on the settings are not fully utilizing the capabilities of the PC as a gaming platform. On the up side, at least gamers with not so powerful systems can still enjoy the game and have fun.

- [b]Disappointing Boss Fight (NO SPOILERS):[/b] -A certain boss fight for me was very disappointing since it was more or less a quick time event and mini-game than an actual fight. The fight in itself was still badass and manly as hell with regards to the story though.

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
GREAT GAME, extremely fun and satisfying to play with a very enjoyable singleplayer and multiplayer experience.

[h1]WORTH IT?:[/h1]
The game is well worth its full price for not just the fans of the Warhammer 40,000 universe but fans of 3rd person action games and new comers to the franchise alike.

Space Marine is a spectacular game. The graphics beautiful and they clearly show the the people who moddled this game took a lot of time and effort on this game. In the campaign I liked to spend 5 minutes sometimes just to admire the scene.  THere aren't many games out their that have been given as much time and effort to make the background so inspiring and so real life. Not only it shows the Imperium of man in the 41st millennium have such skilled builders like described in the books, but also shows how much potential moddlers can achieve when creating the game people are going to play.

The combat system is amazing. When first I heard about a 3rd person shooter for warhammer 40k I first thought it was a mistake and it should of been a first person. But I'm gladly they didn't make it a first person shooter, because if so the game would of been completley different. Not only it allows you to see background the full scale of the war, but also the executions you just can't stop loving. Every close combat weapon have there own executions for different scenarios of combat and for both Orc and Chaos as well as the Chaos deamons.

The campaign is a thrilling adventure which you can't stop playing until you have to force yourself to take a break. Like some books that have such cliff hangers on every chapter you can't stop reading, for example: Percy Jackson. There are scenes which hold your breath because you don't know where the squids will come from (little Orc kamikaze peach dogs that go up to their enemies and explode in front of their face) as your in a tight spaced sewer that the Orcs use to get into places. You don't know if they'l go up behind you or not and if they do then they can make you jump resulting in you getting killed sometimes, (which happened to me a lot in one of the chapters). There are also very happy ending like you finnaly beating the Orc warcheif and stop having to fight with the orcs.
There are two bosses in the game: The Orc Warcheif and The Chaos Prince, who both have their own combat moves which you have to get fiqure out and make a plan how to counter them. 
There is only one sidequest in the game: to collect all servo sulls. It's not necessarily quest because no-one gives it to you, but there are to achivements if you collect servo skulls. And each servo skull is reward. Hint: It's something to do with Imperial Guard the and the people when the Orc Invasion struck. 

After you finnish the campaign, you really want to go and start playing online. There are 2 gamemodes: Versus and Exterminatus.
Versus contains different gamemodes where there 2 teams against each oother: seize ground, annihilation, capture the flag, and a dlc gamemode: Drednought.
Seize ground is where there are 3-4 control points and both team have to hold and defend control points from the enemy team whilest treing to capture the enemies. Each control point you hold gives you points unless the enemy have captured more control points than your team.
Annihilation is where both teams try to be the first to get 41 kills.
Capture the flag is where both teams have to defend their own flag and capture the enemies flag 3 times.
Drednought is where both teams battle out to be in control of a drednought. At the start of the game or whenever a drednought is destroyed there will only be on capture point. The team who capture it, one of their players will become a drednought. That team has to captaure as many points as possible until reaching 20 points, whilest the other team try to destroy the drednought and dfending the control points.
Versus also contains weapon and armor challenges. Whenever you complete enough weapon points for a specific weapon, you get a weapon perk for that weapon. If you complete enough armour challenges, you get different armour parts available to you for you to use.

Exterminatus is really fun. There are a max of 4 players in a single game, where they need to work as a team treing to survive waves of Orcs or Imperial guard or Space Marines. There are 2 exterminatus gamemodes and 3 maps. Each map contains 4 arenas and each arena contains 5 waves. The 4th arena however has a bonus round.

What I always liked about this game was the simplicity of the experience. You're a Space Marine. There are orks. You kill orks. For the Emperor. 

If you don't already know Warhammer 40k, here's the deal: 40,000 years into the future, the human Imperium worships their God-Emperor (he didn't exactly want the job of being called God), and spans a million worlds. There's several alien species which would be happy to exterminate humanity (and each other), as well as a sort of parallel-dimension-spirit-world that can corrupt things on this side. 

In this, you play as a Space Marine: A genetically and surgically augmented supersoldier who can live for centuries (but will probably be killed in battle before then), and has some thoughtful extras like three lungs and two hearts and their skeletal growth includes their ribcage fusing into a essential a solid sheet for better organ protection. Then they're put into armor that makes them even stronger and faster. Right, you play as one of them. And you're given a gun that shoots small rocket-propelled grenades designed to penetrate then explode inside the target, and given a chainsword (that is, a chainsaw with a hilt).

Gameplay switches between God-of-War-esque Beat-em-Up action and over-the-shoulder-shooter very smoothly, and it needs to; you'll run into mixed groups of ranged and melee enemies pretty quickly. Difficulty is a surprisingly natural curve, too. You'll see enemies who need specialized moves or combos to defeat--you might encounter one by itself the first time, and then after that you'll run into a group of three or four. As the game goes on, things escalate and early-game enemies aren't ever quite obsolete. Another nice touch is your health regen is accomplished by doing execution-type kills on stunned enemies. There aren't health pickups; if you're on low health you have to charge something and prove hard enough.

This is one of those definite "grab it on sale" games. Gameplay is simple, but it's fun and challenging.

Space Marine is one of the only Warhammer games other than DoW to break the 40k curse. While there are other decent entries into 40k's growing video game lineup, most suffer from a somewhat cliche storyline, or mediocre game mechanics.

First off, the fact you play as Ultramarines might throw some off from even giving this game the time of day, but I'm telling you now that Captain Titus is the most badass Ultramarine you can play as. You land on a forge world in the beginning of the campaign in response to an ork invasion and to retake a captured manufactorum holding a Warlord class titan. 

The gameplay you're treated to is a mix of a 3rd person shooter and hack'n'slash, and the game handles it very well. Ranged weapons have solid sound design and hit with the impact you'd expect from a fully automatic .75 caliber rocket launcher, and melee weapons all have the weight behind them to back up the power that you force onto your unwilling Xenos test subjects. It's gritty, bloody, gory, and oh so satisfying. Refill your health by brutally executing your enemies, and the amount of health you gain back is directly tied to how big the enemy is, just make sure you're not getting swarmed when executing because enemies will still attack you. As for difficulty, the game itself is not excrutiatingly difficult on hard, but it does provide a healthy challenge and makes you change your tactics dependent on what mistake you made last try. Enemies will hit harder and be more aggressive on higher difficulties, much akin to how Orks really are.

After you finish the about 8-10 hour campaign, you can take the fight online, although not so much anymore. Right now the only mode you'll find populated is Sieze Ground which is basically Conquest from Battlefield, but there's enough players to make matches, even though you'll likely see the same group of players almost every time. Matches are 8v8 with Space Marines vs Chaos Space Marines, and you can customize your character by either using a pre-made chapter color scheme, a pre-made chapter oriented set of armor, or you can make your own with a massive array of armor pieces, colors, emblems, and trimmings to make a massive 1.8 billion possibilities. You can customize your classes with weapons and perks, including weapon specific perks you achieve by using whichever weapon of your choice (bolter with kraken/targeter OP). There are 3 distinct classes in Multiplayer, the all-around tactical, the melee oriented Assault with a jump pack, and the heavy weapon specialist Devastators. Each class has a couple unique traits to help with their playstyle. Tactical has the fastest sprint speed with normal shields, Assault has weaker shields in exchange for increased mobility with its jump pack, and Devastators have the strongest shields to help compensate for their slow movement speed. When there is a good group of players in a game, it can be a helluva lot of fun, but sadly the multiplayer is mostly dead right now. 

Space Marine is possibly the best shooter in 40k's lineup and is very fun to play. The campaign, while not stellar, is certainly worth playing through the end. Although if you want this for multiplayer, I'd have to give it a pass unless you have a clan or something to play with.

Warhammer 40K: Space Marine is one of those rare games that grabs you from the first second and never lets go. From the moment you drop onto the forge world of Graia as Captain Titus, it's pure, glorious mayhem—and it feels incredible.

This game doesn’t mess around with hiding behind cover or recharging shields. No, you're charging into waves of Orks and Chaos like a walking tank, chainsword roaring in one hand and bolter thunder in the other. It's the ultimate power fantasy, and man, does it deliver.

The combat is where it really shines. The seamless blend of ranged and melee combat is just chef’s kiss. Executions aren't just flashy—they’re how you stay alive. The more aggressive you are, the better you do. Every hit, every gunshot, every takedown feels chunky and satisfying. Few games get this level of weight and impact so right.

The story is straightforward, but that’s all it needs. It leans deep into that gritty, gothic Warhammer 40K aesthetic with jaw-dropping environments, thick atmosphere, and just the right amount of lore to pull you in—whether you’re a diehard fan or totally new. The voice acting slaps too—Titus is the definition of “calm, collected, and kills everything.”

Even all these years later, the visuals still look amazing, and the soundtrack is pure epic war hymn material. It pumps you up. It wants you to crush xenos beneath your boots.

And let’s not forget the multiplayer. Exterminatus mode was criminally underrated—fighting off waves of enemies with a custom Marine was a blast, and it absolutely deserved more love and support.

Games like this don’t come around often. Space Marine is unapologetically bold, brutally fun, and just an absolute joy to play. We need more games like this—games that embrace their tone, respect the player’s time, and just let you go nuts in a beautifully crafted world.

With Space Marine 2 finally here, there’s no better time to jump back in. This isn’t just a great Warhammer title—it’s one of the most fun action games ever made. Period.

So I was looking through my list of owned games and realized I don't have anything with a hero or main protagonist as incredibly badass as Captain Titus from [b]Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine[/b]. I then made a ranking: second place is tied between Batman and Strider Hiryu while fourth place goes to the Boss from [b]Saints Row the Third[/b] who narrowly edges out The Overlord for possessing better minions. This list isn't up for debate nor is it the topic of this review, though. The topic is how playing such an overpowering character can be an experience in itself.
 
You are for all intent and purposes a giant superhuman walking tank whose main weapons are a fully automatic mini-rocket launcher and a chainsaw sword. You fly around on a rocket pack coming down with a hammer that produces an explosion of concussive force. You heal yourself in the blood and guts of your broken opponents. You can literally run through some of your lesser enemies. None of this makes the game a cakewalk: orks will mob you relentlessly with their oversized choppers, chaos forces have access to plasma cannons and there are always monsters greater in size than you. It doesn't matter. Being such a superhuman badass just pushes you to greater acts of heroism.
 
The gameplay is basic but enjoyable enough: fire those bolt shells, melee the shooters, dodge roll a lot, throw a grenade into that mess of orks, use the Rage gauge before you die... The difference is that being in control of Captain Titus makes all of this [i]so satisfying.[/i] There is weight in your run. The ground thumps as you do your dodge roll. Your bolter feels like the mini-rocket launcher it's supposed to be and not some standard machine gun. The execution scenes are barbaric, gruesome and as bloody as any [b]Mortal Kombat[/b] Fatality. It [i]enhances[/i] the gameplay, giving every one of your actions greater impact.
 
At this point, I should state that no knowledge of the Warhammer 40K lore is required to get into [b]Space Marine[/b]. What more, if by some strange circumstance you're a Warhammer enthusiast or a lapsed fan who has not yet bought the game, I can honestly say that THQ have written an Ultramarine Captain better than the current in-house team of writers. Again: the story is basic enough in a "save the empire" kind of manner but it's the glorious yet still humble Captain Titus who draws you in.
 
This is actually the main shortcoming of this game. Outside of the main story you have Multiplayer Mode WHERE YOU DO NOT control Captain Titus, playing instead as a bog standard space marine. Instead of orks you face other space marines where you'll find yourself dying in seconds to lascannons, meltaguns and insta-kill thunder hammers; often with no knowledge over how you could've prevented your death. [b][u]The Good[/u][/b]:
[list]
[*]The story was more interesting than I thought it would be.

[*]There is a community that plays the multiplayer regularly.
[*]Customize the look of your character for MP and co-op. Make them look like they are from a pre-existing chapter, or invent your own.
[*]There’s a decent weapon variety, but you can only hold 4 weapons at once and certain weapons replace others.
[*]The soundtrack definitely fits the game and goes from tracks that say “determined” to “ heresy” to “all hope is lost” to “get off of my planet”.
[*]Constant blood eruptions from the ork hordes as you tear into them with steel and lead. I’m a fan of the [b]Orcs Must Die[/b] series, so you know I’m all about that.
[*]If you want your health back, you have to earn it. Regain health by brutalizing your enemies with an execution.
[/list]

[b][u]The Neutral[/u][/b]:
[list]
[*]The overworld is bleak, brown, dusty, and apocalyptic. This may turn off some people, but it fits and it’s not all you see the entire game.
[*]The game could have used more sensitivity options. When I set it to my liking for normal movement/weapons, it’s too fast for sniper scopes. The sensitivity isn’t too high to where it becomes obnoxious, but it’s not as precise as I would want it. Sensitivity buttons on the mouse helps.
[/list]

[b][u]The Bad[/u][/b]:
[list]
[*]If you want to 100% the game, it’s going to be a grind. Most weapons have challenges to complete, and while there is a community keeping the multiplayer alive, it would be near impossible to do them all in actual games. You’ll need grinding buddies; and I’m not talking about the fun kind.
[*]Again, if you’re going for 100%, you’ll have to get 40,000 kills. It’s quite the grind, but there are three methods you can use:[olist]
[*]Use the TRENCHES checkpoint under Chapter 2 and work your way to the turret. Kill all but one of the enemies with it and then restart from checkpoint. You’ll load in relatively close to the turret instead of the original checkpoint. This method will grant you 50-60 kills each time.
[*]Use the FALLEN BROTHER checkpoint under Chapter 14. Pick up the autocannon and shoot the endless waves of enemies as they spawn. The autocannon has 400 bullets, so you’ll have to reload the checkpoint when it runs out.
[*]Load up a private game of Exterminatus, choose Arena 1 under Hab Center. If you can make it to the end of wave 5, you’ll have around 700 kills. Die before the wave ends instead of proceeding to Arena 2, then rinse and repeat.
[/olist][/list]
[*]There’s a lot of camera shake. If that bothers you, you may have to enjoy this game in small doses.

[b][u]Pro Tips[/u][/b]:

[list][*]Small enemies don’t need to be stunned to execute them.
[*]Stronger enemies require a different combo to stun them so they can be executed (melee, melee, kick instead of just kick, for example).
[/list]

I really enjoy this game. It's pretty much mindless fun most of the time. The game's divided in 3 different game modes, or so I feel, let's try to quickly analize each mode, shall we?

First, we got the single player campaign. The game stars Captain Titus, probably the only likable Ultramarine out there, in a short-ish action packed, VERY linear third person shooter campaign. The way it often goes is, move from point A to point B, reach a big arena where enemies try to bumrush you, kill everyone in there in the name of the Emperor, and move to the next arena, killing a few stray enemies on the way. You can carry 4 weapons at a time, not counting melee weapons, a pistol, a heavy weapon, a normal weapon, and a bolter. The weapons featured in the game are pretty much what you'd expect from the Spess Mahreens. You got a bolter, bolt pistol and a storm bolter, a heavy bolter, plasma cannon, gun and pistol, lascannon, VENGEANCE LAUNCHER (which is basically a stickybomb launcher), a melta (Which is pretty much a shotgun in this game. Why? I dunno), a stalker bolter, a chainsword, hammer, and power axe. Sadly, there are no lightning claws or power fists. In this game, there is no such thing as health regen or medkits, the enemies ARE the medkits. When you stun an enemy, either by bitchslapping them or hurting them enough, they are open for a brutal, awesome execution, which in turn, heals you. Did anybody say blood for the blood god? 

The campaign itself is quite linear, and you got AI teammates following you around most of the time, and it feels a bit generic at times, but hey, I think that's what they were aiming for. After all, the Ultramarines do feel like generic action heroes. There's a harder difficulty, but honestly, it wasn't too challenging either. 

Then, we move to the multiplayer half of the game. 

First, we got Exterminatus, which is basically last stand from Retribution, with 4 players instead of 3,  but with only space marines fighting against 20 waves of orks, and a final wave of chaos. You can customize your loadout, customize your perks, and go for it. Each 5 waves, you move to a different location, depending on the arena you're playing on, and there's 2 currently in the base exterminatus mode. 
The DLC Chaos Unleashed adds another arena, and allows you to play as chaos. I feel like this DLC really shakes things up, since now the imperial guard and space marines are included as enemies in the game, and orks still spawn, so there are times where it's utter chaos since all 3 factions are trying to kill each other. This arena though, is REALLY challenging compared to the base Exterminatus mode. Sadly, I find it impossible to find a match unless I'm playing with friends in this mode. And what's really annoying is, the game doesn't allow you to just search Chaos Unleashed lobbies, it forces you to search for both regular and chaos lobbies, so most of the time, you're just gonna get regular.
Exterminatus is not too bad, but honestly, I feel like once you are able to clear all of the arenas, there's not much else to it.
In Exterminatus, you do level up your multiplayer rank, but you do not unlock any of the weapon attachements here, for that, you need play the regular multiplayer. 

And now, the final part of the game, the PvP multiplayer. This. This is where I've spent most of my time in this game. It's really, really basic honestly, you got a few maps, 3 classes (Assault (Melee and jetpack oriented class), devastator/havoc(Heavy weapons, either a sniper, a machinegunner, or a rocket launcher of sorts)  and tactical (Most general assault rifles and weapons like that, if we compare them to other multiplayer shooters), a few perks, a few weapons, and two add ons for most (Except the pistols) that are unlocked by either killing enemies with a certain weapon for one, and doing other random stuff for the other (Like multi kills for the plasma cannon or killstreaks for the bolter).

There's also a few game modes, but the most played are 3 or 4 control point matches, or team deathmatch. There's a mode that adds dreadnoughts to the game, but it's dead as shit, your only chance to play this is purchasing the DLC AND gathering a bunch of friends to play it. But honestly, I found it quite fun.

Honestly, there's not a lot of content in this mode, but it still feels really satisfying. The combat feels rather responsive and the hits are so beefy that it just feels good to hit people in this game, and most weapons kill you rather fast so you gotta stay on your toes and dodge frequently or use cover. The combat is responsive....When there are not any lag issues. 

Yep, this is one of those games. It does not use servers for the multiplayer, it uses peer to peer, and while it does have all of the issues you'd expect from that (If the host's got a bad internet connection, everybody else suffers, and constant host migration interrupting the game IN THE WORST POSSIBLE MOMENTS), it's honestly the only reason of why this game is still alive to this day. 

I personally found two issues with the multiplayer portion of this game. The first is, there's not a lot of customization. Sure, each weapon's got 1 to 2 add ons, and you got 2 perks per class, but some of the weapons and perks are SO meta (And the meta is stale, no updates, it will never change) that there's at least 1 necessary perk per class that is pretty much a must have, leaving little room for experimenting, unless you don't mind not following the meta. Most of the matches you'll face people using the same perks and the same weapons, and a FUCKTON of lascannons, which I feel like it's kinda broken in this game, since it fires too fast and it's too damn accurate, making the stalker bolter feel a bit pointless at times in my opinion. 

The second issue with this game is, well, it really happens in any game with a small community. The skill gap is HUGE, you'll find two kinds of players, the ones who are brand new to the game and suck, and the ones who have been playing for hundreds of thousands of hours, and sometimes the teams are stacked and if you are a new player in this situation, I understand if you don't want to play it. I personally found myself in the situation where I was being constantly bullied by other players, and I just had to adapt and try to get good no matter what, and I felt like it did kinda pay off. 

All in all, I definitely recommend this game if you are a fan of 40k, or third person shooters,  since honestly we don't have a lot of good 40k games here on steam. If you don't mind the content being a bit repetitive at times, you'll probably have fun with this. If you are turned off by the lack of maps, lack of weapons, and lack of content in general, and you are expecting 20+ maps in a multiplayer game, then this might not be for you. This game certainly feels like DoW 1, the vanilla version. There's not a lot of content, but that's because this was supposed to be a trilogy, which sadly got cancelled after the studio behind it died. I'd say give it a try, specially if it's on sale.

I'll just say this really quick: Warhammer 40K: Space Marine is a fun game. It's only weaknesses aren't necessarily things it did wrong, but that it couldn't expand upon what it had leaving me with a sense "it could have been so much more!"

Rather than listing pros and cons I think it'd be better to discuss things in sections, no story spoilers!

[Gameplay]:

Shooting: Shooting in this game is just fine. Not ground breaking but mechanically sound. You have a pistol and asault rifle basicaly for all of the game which get upgraded. Your other two weapon slots are reserved for a variety of other weapons in the game, some of which can't be held in conjunction with others. You never feel under armed and there was plenty of tactical choise as well guns were usefull in the right circumstances (and looked damn cool). This game also isn't stingy with your ammo capacity, you only keep running to ammo crates because you keep expanding lots of ammo but yet never feel like you are purposesly being capped low.

The main weakness of shooting is that it felt like it needed  a cover system. Hiding behind certain objects without the ability to duck was annoying at times. The right stick for mostly unused for clicking except for one weapon to change the zoom level while using its scope. Otherwise it was free.

Melee: There are three weapons in the game and both felt mighty and powerful. The chainsword was, IMO, great for fast attacks with a good single target DPS. The axe was slower and IDK how well it did for single target damage, but many of its combos did broad sweeps hitting multipel enemies at once. Basically good soft AOE. The hammer hit the hardest, some attacks could hit multipel targets if times adn aimed right and it could stagger some enemies. Main weakness was that it was also slow and the game didn't let you use any guns other than your pistol and AR type weapon. Basically a situational thing.

Melee's main weakness was that it wasn't developed enough. Each weapon had five combo attacks. There was a basic attack button, a stun (which only worked when an enemy could be sent into the execution state), an execution to gain back base health (there was also a rechargable energy shield) and a dodge roll. The stun didn't do much unless it was part of a combo, and even then it was only effective if the enemy's health was low enough to be ready to be executed. There were painfully few executions; each weapon had effectively two animations for basic (AKA the weaker orcs you see throughout the game) and only one for stronger (AKA later game enemies that constitute all enemies eventually) enemies. 

As amusing as it was to slam a hammer into an orc's balls and watch Titus reach into its mouth to rip its skull apart, it got old.

Dodge roll was servicable for shooting combat but felt slow and not swiftly responsive for melee use. It also didn't knock enemies out of your way despite Titus being heavy and strong enough to do so against most. 

The lack of a counter/block/parry system really hurt melee combat. The game felt like such a thing belonged in it and some enemies charge you, can't get staggered normally and have lots of health so it takes a lot to get them ready for execute. Since I couldn't counter there attacks I often died if I tried to fight them head on so I kept running back to shoot at them. Melee really did not seem as strong as it should have been.

The Fury Mode: Fury mode had a bar that filled as you did damage. Once activated it made your melee attacks stronger or, if you aimed time slowed down to make you a better shot. Problem was that slow-mo didn't feel usefull except for a few times. Since melee combat wasn't strong I wasn't confident in using it.

Its main utility was to regenerate your base health. However, I am a rather silly person and managed to not notice this until I was almost done with the game. :(

[Level Design]:

Initially the levels were pretty neat, big epic spralling landscapes, huge buildings, etc. Except the game didn't really have much else. The environments got old and the set pieces for fights got reused over and over again. These areas weren't bad, but they just got old. It didn't help that there weren't enough enemy types. I got sick of fighting the orcs by the time another faction showed up and they got old by the last couple of levels as well.

There were also long stretches were the environment didn't change at all, no story bits happened or character quips, so fighting room after room of enemies got tedious. While the game actually has a large variety of things it gave you to do, it also had to pad itself too much.

There were a couple of boss fights but nothing of worth. Mechanics weren't really there, just bullet sponges who three mooks at you to keep things interesting. I'll forget their names by tomorrow, and within the next couple of days to a week I won't even remember what they looked like. It's not like there aesthetic design was bad, there just wasn't enough character there to remember.

[Story]:

The story was only okay. I've only read about WH40K before so some stuff at the beginning was nice because it was unfamiliar. Maybe some later stuff would have been more interesiting if I was knowledgable but for a series novice I just didn't see it. It did have a great premise and bullet point plot though so with some eleboration and added bits it could have been a fine story.

There were some collectable audio logs but as they were really just letting you know other people were getting killed besides you. Some side bits were interesting but I've already forgotten a bunch of them.

Length-wise I beat it in 10-11 hours on the hardest difficulty, though the game definately felt padded to get itself that long. Note that I didn't try too hard to find the collectable audio logs so I'm guessing this is close to average.

[Acting]:

Was only okay. Some characters didn't have good actors. Others felt like their actors could be decent if given better direction for tonal and emotional range.

[Most Dissappointing]:

During the early game you get a huge mech shown off in the background. I was looking forward to piloting it but the actual level it was involved in just had me help super charge its weapon by the time it left its hangar bay. Gross dissappointment but understandable as described in my silver lining.

[Silver Lining]:

This game was only Okay to Semi-Good because it didn't expand itself enough. IMO that's the best kind of an "Okay" game!

While there were lots of corners cut I felt like the devs tried there best to minimize those the best they could with their tiem and resources. The mech was huge, like if Godzilla monsters had a size scale it would be on the lower end of it.

In order to pilot it they would have needed a whole new environment for a level design, animations, as well enemies other than the orc gunship that could have been a threat. In order to introduce these enemies they also would have needed to tease them early on so they don't come out of nowhere.

Enemies felt varied believe it or not for this level of effort. As did the combat, weapon variety, mechanics and AI. 

This game only needed a bigger budget and dev team, with maybe a better writer or at least the man or woman a chance to write a longer story.

When people this has aged well, they aren't kidding. And to reiterate, I liked it despite it's flaws. 

It was, above all else, FUN!

[My Hopes]:

From what I've found this game didn't sell well originally, and since the dev also makes the Dawn of War RTS series they refocused on that. 

However, my searches have shown that 4-5 WH40K games have released in the last 1-2 years and they've been either Okay, Mediocre or Terrible. 

Since this game ends on a cliff hanger we may never know what happens to Titus. But given that it, and the first two Dawns of War, are the best selling and best reviewed games we may see them announce a sequel in the future. Definately worth a buy for the right price!

This game is probably the closest we've come to having a good Warhammer 40k title in a very long time, which is probably to be expected since this is a Relic title from the good days of Relic, before the "we must appeal to the wider audience!" nonsense made them ruin DoW3. While I don't have too many hours logged here on Steam, I have played this game extensively on console.

+Positives:

-The game without a doubt nails the feel of 40k. You're surrounded by Gothic architecture, people in British accents, explosions, and general carnage and death. The manufactorums blare constant messages to long dead workers, telling them to continue working for the glory of the Emperor and the Machine God. It's everything you would expect a 40k game's atmosphere to be.

-The weapons sound beautiful. Bolters sound like the automatic cannons that they are, chainswords rip and tear gloriously, Space Marines thud and shake the ground as they charge around like the walking tanks they are. 

-Weapons feel right. They feel heavy and impactful. Bolter fire creates showers of blood and gore as .75 cal explosive rounds tear through bodies, each swing from your chainsword rips your enemies apart and absolutely drenches you in blood. Nothing feels like a nerf gun pretending to be a real gun.

-There is no health regen unless you're near death, and even then it's only about a quarter of your health bar. You want to heal? You heal by giving an Ork a chainsaw vasectomy. You want a health pack? Punch a Gretchin until it explodes. It only takes one punch. There's also a Fury mode which you can activate to gain health regen and increased melee damage after you rip and tear enough to please the Emperor.

-You're fairly durable. You're a Space Marine, wearing some of the best armor ever developed. You feel like a tank, but you aren't invincible. You can tear through hordes of smaller Orks without breaking stride, but fights between other Marines or large orks can go badly quickly if you get overconfidant. When you fight traitor marines, or other players in multiplayer, it feels like a clash between titans instead of a fight between mortals.

-The voice acting is on point. Mark Strong is fantastic as Captain Titus, and his squadmates voices were also well chosen. The voices for the enemy NPCs and the few other friendly NPCs are also fairly good.

-The story is decent. It's not going to win any awards, and if you know anything about 40k (or even if you don't) you'll probably be able to guess some of the plot points before they happen. That said, the story doesn't hurt the game and it's still possible to get interested and invested in the characters. You won't leave the game asking any deep, meaningful questions, but you also won't leave the game regreting your purchase. There are plenty of awesome moments, some cool dialogue, everything you'd expect to come out of 40k. The story fits the game. It's good, fairly simple, and pretty enjoyable.

-It controls well. The options menu isn't huge, but the controls are intelligent for the most part. It's not a game that you'll need an extra hand to play, and it works well on both keyboard and controller.


=Neutral:


-The multiplayer is pretty simple. Deathmatch, CTF, etc. The usual game modes. It's not as good as the single player, but it's a servicable time-sink if you want to shoot other players in a 40k game. Some single player mechanics are removed or changed to make them work in a multiplayer setting, but overall it's still decent.

-There is a co-op PVE mode, but it's very hard. It's a round-based game where you have to hold an arena against waves of Orks and eventually Chaos, with the waves going up in difficulty until you reach what is essentially an unbeatable last wave. I've only beaten it once, and we had a hacker playing with us who had unlimited ammo and was invincible. It's a fun mode, but it can get repetitive after a while.


-Negatives:

-The multiplayer is basically dead. The game is so old, and the actual multiplayer content is so basic and small that there aren't a whole lot of people still playing. The game also runs peer to peer instead of on a dedicated server, which can be seen as a blessing or a curse since, while you have to deal with all the problems that come from having the match running off of one of the players internet (so if he's far away or has bad internet you can have terrible ping), it also means that there are no servers to be shut down.

-The multiplayer modes can get boring quickly. There's a few maps, a few modes, and the co-op has even less in the way of options.

-There are hackers. Pretty much explains itself.

-You can't choose which faction you play as. You're randomly assigned to either Chaos or Loyalist when you join a match. While it doesn't effect the gameplay, since the wargear for both factions is stat identical save for flavor like chainaxes instead of power axes and daemon mauls instead of thunder hammers, you can't work towards cosmetics for one faction while playing the other. So if you really want a certain piece of armor for your Loyalist marine, but you keep getting put on the Chaos team, there's nothing you can do about it. You can't even switch teams once you're in the match.

-The campaign is very linear. While it's not entirely a bad thing, it does mean that there's not as much replayability as a more option game.


Overall, the game is good. It has a solid single player, and a decent multiplayer. Though you can easily tell it was made with the single player as top priority, the rest of the game can be enjoyable if you can find a community that still plays this game, or you have friends that do.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is pretty cool I guess.

Set in the distant future where mankind decided that skulls on everything was totally in. The Imperium of Man has spread thoughout the known galaxy with the guidance of a super powered god-like figure known as the Emperor of Mankind. But the Emperor was betrayed by his favored son, Horus, and after a bloody civil war and the defeat of Horus, the Emperor was left as a crippled body upon a golden throne, which is the only thing that's keeping him alive. 
Now 10,000 years later, humanity is beset on all sides by mutants, aliens, and the forces of Chaos. 

But it's not all hopeless, for the armies of mankind also have the Space Marines! genetically altered and augmented super soldiers clad in power armor and armed with weapons that would break your arm if you as much as tried to use them. These Space Marines are split into chapters, and no chapter is greater than the Ultramarines, warriors who lead and try to set an example for all Space Marines to follow. 

So basically they're the brown-nosing nerds of the 40k Universe.

You play as Titus, a Space Marine captain of the Ultramarines. Which is to say he's the star quarterback on a team made entirely out of quarterbacks. You and your team of similarly jacked super soldiers are deployed on the planet Graia, a Forgeworld that focuses on military development as well as the development of super cool giant robots! Graia is under attack by Orks, a war-like race of fungus based aliens that consist entirely of soccer hooligans that come in sizes ranging from big to Big to BIG. Also little Goblins called Gretchins, but they don't matter. 
Titus must secure the giant robot making factory so that the orks don't strip down the giant robot sitting inside for parts. Which would be...Heresy? I think? 

Yeah, heresy! 

Space Marine is a third person shooter with an emphasis on getting down and dirty with your enemy. Which is sexy, but also not. You are given a plethora of weapons to carry, as well as a choice of melee weapon for when you have to put your arms up at 10 and 2 against the alien scumbags. While your weapons fill most of the essential shooter roles, one stands out the most, which is your standard issue Bolter, which is an assault  weapon that fires .75 calibre rounds which are explosive tipped and rocket propelled. 

I don't think understand what I just said. You are essentially firing the fist of an angry at anything dumb enough to not be born human, and sometimes humans as well because screw em. 

But sometimes the orks get close and you have to have a strong word with them, and what better way to do that then with a chainsword. A chainsaw sword.
A sword that doubles as a chainsaw.
It's a chainsaw on a stick.
Am I even getting through to you right now? 

Not only do you have a Chainsword, but you also have a power axe, a weapon covered in a blue-hazy force field THAT IS CAPABLE OF DISRUPTING THE MOLECULAR BONDS OF MATTER WHEN IT STRIKES
And a thunder hammer, a giant hammer... Also it explodes. 

How the game works is that you mix your two styles of combat together, engaging your enemies from a distance with your ranged weapons and then closing in with your melee weapon to give them a stern talking to.
And by that I mean murder. 

Your enemies will always outnumber you, so 9 times out of 10 you're going to be in melee combat anyway. The melee itself isn't all that impressive, you have an attack button and you have a stun button, but you can also grab stunned enemies and turn them into a fine red paste for health. That's the only way you can get your health back, you execute the stunned enemies in a gory fashion which refills your health like you're some sort of buff vampire.

Or you can get really mad  for a few seconds and let your health refill that way. 

Luckily, the weapons in this game are crunchy enough to feel rewarding for every playstyle so don't be afraid to mix it up. You're going to get into melee combat, either way. So at least the weapons feel nice to use. 

Titus himself, as a Space Marine, is a pretty heavy fellow, but don't say that to his face because you might hurt his feelings, and Titus is a nice guy. You monster.
Oh yeah, also he can kill you. 

The Space Marines move with weighted thuds to every one of their steps, making them seem like lumbering oafs at first, until you get Titus to go into a charge. Now he's like a rip roaring retard rhino that can smash down everything in his way. Space Marines are surprisingly agile for their size, but I guess that comes with the whole Super Soldier thing. You'd think that at least their pauldrons get in the way, but they don't seem to have a problem with them. 

But should you play Battlemallet 40,000: Star Guys? 

It's pretty good, especially if it's on sale. I haven't played the multiplayer since it came out, but I remember having a little fun with that as well, so you at least have some staying power with the game, if people even still play. The 40k universe itself is fairly unique and the dialogue and characteristics of the characters might actually catch you off guard if you aren't familiar with the source material. 

I would say check it out, it's nothing amazing but it's still fun to play. The game can drag on near the end, which is a complaint I've been having a lot recently. Where a new enemy type basically forces you through a gauntlet of rooms filled with them before you can reach the end. It kind of feels like they almost ran over their dead line making this game since the last part of the game has encounters the game itself isn't really built for. Space marines in this game don't take cover, and there's a lot of shooting going on near the end.

"Space Marine" is a short experience but full of action. You take on the role of badass Space Marine, equipped with a diverse range of weapons to complete your mission. It mixes and matches melee with ranged combat in a way that allows you to take full control of the battlefield. 

I found myself feeling like I was playing a DOOM game, with an array of different weapons to massacre hundreds of enemies, executions to recover health, etc. It has a ton of its own personality, like being third person and having heavier movement, but the action-filled feeling is all the same. Combat is hard, but as you progress and gain experience, you start identifying enemies' weaknesses and how to deal with them. Each weapon serves its purpose, and you're going to have an easier time if you choose your loadout correctly. Shooting and melee combat both feel only mediocre at best. 

The story is passable, it just follows the same formula already done tons of times. Graphics for a 2011 release hold up remarkably well today. Sound design also felt good. 

I'm excited to try out its sequel and see what Captain Titus is up to these days.

Note: This game been tried out and reviewed in Steam offline mode or on Consoles.
